sources.note: No phonology at all; lists dialects Abgue, Agrab, Duguri, Eastern Birgit and the three references (Jungraithmayr 2004, 2005; Marti et al. 2007).

sources.citation: Jungraithmayr, Herrmann. 2024. Emergenz und Genese der Tonalität im Tschadischen: Ein Beitrag zur Sprachgeschichte Nordostafrikas. Folia Orientalia 61. DOI 10.24425/for.2024.152390
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Comparative essay on the rise of tone in Chadic; a full-text search for stress/accent and read of the East Chadic passages show it discusses Mubi ('eine tonale Struktur.. mit zwei Tonebenen', p. 169) and Masmaje, never Birgit; no statement about stress/accent for any language.

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.1 languoid page birg1239 and reference records 156811, 62955, 131568
sources.note: Bibliography only: no descriptive-grammar entry for Birgit (Glottolog lists no grammar, sketch or phonology); Jungraithmayr 2004 typed 'wordlist', Marti et al. 2007 'overview;wordlist;socling'. Nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Alio, Khalil. 2004. Préliminaires à une étude de la langue kajakse d'Am-Dam, de toram du Salamat, d'ubi du Guéra et de masmaje du Batha-est (Tchad). In Takács (ed.), Egyptian and Semito-Hamitic (Afro-Asiatic) Studies in Memoriam Werner Vycichl, 229–285. Leiden: Brill.

sources.note: Sketches of Birgit's closest relatives (Kajakse, Masmaje, Toram) by a native East-Chadic linguist; establishes the Mubi-group prosodic type (tone vs. accent) against which a Birgit statement should be read.

sources.citation: Jungraithmayr, Herrmann. 2004. Das Birgit, eine osttschadische Sprache — Vokabular und grammatische Notizen. In Gábor Takács (ed.), Egyptian and Semito-Hamitic (Afro-Asiatic) Studies in Memoriam Werner Vycichl, 342–371. Leiden: Brill.
